voice.text: It rained all day today, and it's cold. [pause] Your friend says: it must be winter! [pause] Can ONE day tell you the season? Tap your guess.
<emphasis>Spring.</emphasis> It warms up. Rain falls. Buds open on the tree. [pause] The fox has kits! And you wear a rain jacket.
<emphasis>Summer.</emphasis> Hot and bright. The tree is full of green leaves. [pause] The fox wears her thin summer coat. You wear a sun hat.
<emphasis>Fall.</emphasis> It cools down. Leaves turn orange and drop. [pause] The fox's coat grows thicker. You put a jacket on.
<emphasis>Winter.</emphasis> Cold. The tree is bare. Snow falls. [pause] The fox wears her thickest coat. You bundle up warm.
But listen. [pause] Inside a season, the weather still changes day by day. A cold rainy day can come in summer. [pause] It is STILL summer!
How do we know the season for sure? [pause] We RECORD the weather, day after day. The pattern shows us.
Look at the clue. [pause] Then tap the best answer.
You read every clue! [pause] Now show what you know.
Not quite. Check the clue again — what do the tree, the animals, and your clothes say?
Not quite. Animals DO feel the seasons. Fur thickens, food is stored, some sleep the winter away.
Not quite. Trees change with the seasons: buds, green leaves, falling leaves, bare.
Not quite. One day is not a season! Daily weather wiggles — the season is the big pattern.
Not quite. Count on the strip, day by day. That's what records are for.
Not quite. It only looks random day by day. Record it, and the pattern appears.
Not quite. Records don't change the weather — they help us SEE its pattern.
Yes! [pause] Bare tree plus snow — that's winter.
Yes! [pause] Animals feel the seasons. Thick coats get ready for winter cold.
Yes! [pause] Spring — everything wakes up and starts growing.
Yes! [pause] In summer the tree is full of green leaves. Bare comes in winter.
Yes! [pause] Daily weather changes inside a season. One cold day doesn't change the season.
Yes! [pause] Count the suns: Monday, Tuesday, Thursday, Saturday. Four sunny days.
Yes! [pause] The strip shows it: four sunny, two rainy. Records let us compare!
Yes! [pause] Day by day looks jumbly — but the record shows the season's pattern.
One hot day comes in spring. Is it summer now?
What does the fox do for winter?
The tree is bare. Which season is it, most likely?
Why do we record the weather every day?
It's fall, and getting cooler. What do people do?
<soft>You can read the seasons!</soft> [pause] Well done.
Good try! Let's watch the meadow once more.
Lesson done! From today, write the season next to the weather in your journal.
